stem.en: A 0.5 kg ball moves along a frictionless track. It starts at rest at point O, where its potential energy is 30 J. At point P its potential energy is 20 J, at Q it is 30 J, and at R it is 40 J. Which statement is correct?

text.en: It reaches P at about 6.3 m/s, Q at 0 m/s, and R at 0 m/s.
It reaches P at 0 m/s, Q at about 6.3 m/s, and never reaches R.
It reaches P at about 6.3 m/s, stops at Q, and never reaches R.
It reaches P, Q and R, at about the same speed of 6.3 m/s.

explanation.en: The total mechanical energy is 30 J. At P, K = 30 - 20 = 10 J, so 1/2 x 0.5 x v^2 = 10 and v = sqrt(40), about 6.3 m/s. At Q, K = 30 - 30 = 0, so the ball stops there. R needs 40 J of potential energy, more than the 30 J total, so the ball never gets there.

hints.en: The total K + U stays 30 J.
Can the ball reach a point where U is more than its total energy?
